questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car, what happens?

options.text: You are in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You stop other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car. This way, the driver will see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What material provides the best protection for riding gloves?
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another strong material to protect your hands.

questions.question: Riding gloves are usually made of what?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They help you grip better and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: In Texas, at what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) are you legally intoxicated?
questions.explanation: In Texas, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means you are legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to drive while intoxicated.

questions.question: What is a simple way to make your motorcycle easier to see?

options.text: Attach a large flag to the frame

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Wear bright, reflective clothing. Use your turn signals and brake light properly so other drivers can see you.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle you have never ridden before, what should you do?

options.text: Check that the seat is comfortable
Assume it is in good condition
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding
Ride normally since most bikes are the same

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding, get familiar with the bike. Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes. Learn the gear pattern.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's brake light compare to a car's brake lights?
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as bright or noticeable as a car's. Flash your brake light before you slow down or stop to help other drivers notice.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. This includes a sturdy jacket, long pants, boots that cover your ankles, and gloves. A stocking cap is not adequate protection.

questions.question: What is important for a helmet to provide the best protection?

options.text: It meets Department of Transportation standards

questions.correctAnswerText: It meets Department of Transportation standards
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly and have no cracks or damage.

questions.question: What is the best gear to wear while riding?
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. This includes a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: Why is a cushion of space helpful when riding?

options.text: It gives you space to react to hazards.
It hides you from other drivers.
It prevents you from avoiding hazards.
It allows you to look at road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you space to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle helps you react quickly if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to steer safely.

questions.question: Why should you keep a good following distance behind other vehicles?

options.text: To give you time and space to spot and react to hazards.
So traffic counters can count you as a vehicle.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give you time and space to spot and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: A good following distance gives you enough space to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also gives you a better view of the road, so you can see hazards like potholes.

questions.question: What should you do if you think stopping your motorcycle will take longer than usual?
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance on slippery surfaces. If your motorcycle will take longer to stop, leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What reduces head and neck injuries?
questions.explanation: A high-quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best defense against injury in a crash.

questions.question: How can you lower your risk of being in a crash?

options.text: Tell other drivers what you are going to do.
Do not look ahead while riding.
Ride in parts of your lane where you are hard to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you are going to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Why should you ride in the left part of your lane when preparing to pass?

options.text: It helps you see farther ahead.
It makes it hard to see past the vehicle.
It lets the other driver speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you see farther ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when preparing to pass. This helps you see farther ahead and makes you more visible to drivers in the passing lane.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take and when should you do it?

options.text: A few minutes and only once a month.
A few minutes and before every ride.
Over an hour and only by a mechanic.
Over an hour and only if you have a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a thorough check of your motorcycle before every ride. It should only take a few minutes.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Ride faster to get away from them.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Change lanes safely and let them get in front of you. Riding faster can make the danger worse by causing them to tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping a group of riders small?

options.text: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
A small group can ignore traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always try to catch up to the group.
It is hard to keep track of where everyone is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
questions.explanation: Small groups have advantages over large groups. They are easier for other vehicles to pass, less likely to be separated by traffic or traffic lights, and do not force slower riders to rush to keep up.
